commits.body:
VF-009 (verification/findings.md): under auto --confirm, JBMC 6.11.0 refutes the conformance corpus's boomTwice and enumBroken at n=0, where the JVM and the tool's own checker hold. Both run a class initializer that throws. The new fixture lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/F.java has one void method per part of the JVM's semantics for such an initializer (JVMS 5.5: the exception wrapped in ExceptionInInitializerError, the class erroneous with NoClassDefFoundError at the next use, the initializer run once, an Error passed through unwrapped), plus copies of the two corpus methods. Every assertion holds on JDK 25.0.5, run inline (java -ea F: 'all hold, runs 4').

Job 20261107-163056-vf-009-triage-a-class-initializer-that-t (priority 10) runs the fixture on stock JBMC with no flags, with --throw-runtime-exceptions, and with the flags jvmcontract passes, prints the goto listings of the two copies, and runs the corpus's methods through jvmcontract prove under --engine jbmc and auto --confirm with their work directories kept. It tells JBMC's semantics from a flag or the adapter's reading of the trace. The fixture README and the cleanup-jbmc brief's Progress say so.
